images.alt: Three boys in denim jackets lean over a pinball machine decorated with moons and flames, in a black and white photo.
images.caption: Boys at a pinball machine during the pinball championships on the Museumplein, Amsterdam, 15 June 1976
images.credit: Rob Bogaerts / Anefo, 1976. CC0, Nationaal Archief, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: Long rows of lit arcade machines in a dim room with red lights and hanging signs for Atari, Taito and Sega/Gremlin.
images.caption: Rows of 1970s and 1980s arcade machines at the American Classic Arcade Museum, Laconia, New Hampshire, USA, 2018
images.credit: Funspotarcade, 2018. CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: Two boys in jumpers stand on a wooden pier, one sorting out a fishing reel, with the bay and a row of palm trees behind them.
images.caption: Two boys fishing from a pier in Melbourne, 1970
images.credit: wilford peloquin, 1970. CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: Children in caps, shorts and school polo shirts sit on a bench eating lunch, with school bags at their feet.
images.caption: Australian and American children take a break at their joint school in Exmouth, Western Australia, August 1989
images.credit: JO1 Lee Bosco, US Navy, 1989. Public domain, US National Archives, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: A round black Simon game with four large buttons, green, red, yellow and blue, in a museum display case.
images.caption: An early Simon electronic game on display at the Henry Ford Museum, Dearborn, Michigan, USA, 2015
images.credit: HarshLight, 2015. CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: A mustard-coloured Hanimex TV game with two black knobs and switches labelled Angle, Speed and Bat size, lying on orange spotted fabric.
images.caption: A Hanimex Colour TV Game from about 1978. Hanimex was an Australian company, and this game has a switch marked ANGLE
images.credit: Bradley Neil (friedorange79), 2018. CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: Black and white photo of a games room: two men play a Super Breakout arcade machine next to a space shooting game, with pinball machines behind them.
images.caption: Super Breakout, Atari's 1978 follow-up to Breakout, being played in the games room at Schiphol Airport, Amsterdam, 18 January 1980
images.credit: Hans van Dijk / Anefo, 1980. CC0, Nationaal Archief, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: A 1977 magazine advertisement with the word HUSTLE in striped orange and purple letters and a wooden arcade cabinet showing a snake game on its screen.
images.caption: A June 1977 trade magazine advertisement for Hustle, Gremlin's follow-up to Blockade
images.credit: Gremlin Industries advertisement, Play Meter, June 1977. Public domain (published without a copyright notice), via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: Close-up of a Space Invaders arcade machine: rows of white aliens and green bunkers on the screen, colourful space artwork around it and a child's hands on the controls.
images.caption: Midway's Space Invaders arcade machine at the Museum of Science and Technology of Catalonia (mNACTEC), Terrassa, Spain, 2012
images.credit: Jordiferrer, 2012. CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: An Atari Asteroids arcade machine with a glowing marquee, a screen showing outline rocks and a tiny ship, and a red and blue button panel.
images.caption: An Atari Asteroids arcade machine at the exhibition Del Tilt al Byte, Valencia, Spain, December 2014
images.credit: Coentor, 2014. CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: A painting of a startled green frog leaping over a red car, above the words Leap for your life and Frogger.
images.caption: A Sega/Gremlin advertisement for Frogger in the American trade magazine Play Meter, 1 December 1981
images.credit: Sega/Gremlin advertisement, Play Meter, 1981. Public domain (no valid copyright notice), via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: A table-top arcade cabinet with a joystick, its glass top showing the blue Pac-Man maze with dots and ghosts.
images.caption: Pac-Man on a table-top arcade cabinet from the Japan Game Museum collection, shown at the Nagoya City Museum, Japan, 2020
images.credit: inunami, 2020. CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.alt: An old computer monitor showing green text: a tall well drawn with brackets and dots, falling blocks made of square brackets, and Russian instructions.
images.caption: The first version of Tetris, with blocks drawn in brackets, at the Lenin Museum in Tampere, Finland, 2022. Its Russian help says keys 7 and 9 move a piece and 8 turns it
images.credit: Unnerving duck, 2022. CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
